title: Cyclone at Savoy — Brenham Weekly Banner, June 4, 1880
text: THE storm king seems to rule supreme; in the entire history of modern times there is nothing on record to compare with the terrible calamities that have ravaged the land during the past few years. The terrible calamity that visited the town of Marshall Mo., docs not compare with that visited on a smaller scale at the village of Savoy, in Fannin county in this state. The latter named town on Saturday last was visited by a terrible rain and wind storm resulting in nearly the destruction of the town and the killing of nine persons. The track of the cyclone was upwards of a quarter of a mile wide and in its course everything was razed to the ground. The people in the devastated district are in a terrible situation and appeal for aid. Citizens in Sherman and Bonham and Clarksville have already responded liberally.
notes: Brief news item. Text is a single paragraph. The cyclone is reported to have killed nine persons and nearly destroyed the town.
